feature1.prompt: Using autodoc_typehints = "description" in Sphinx causes the autoclass directive to include a return type in the generated documentation, even in cases where no return type is expected (for example, in a class constructor such as the Square class). The expected behavior is that no return type should appear for classes. This feature requires a modification to the logic that builds the field list for type annotations so that it can conditionally suppress the return type information when it is not needed.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature focuses on enhancing the internal function that processes type annotations. The modify_field_list function must be updated to accept a new parameter (suppress_rtype) that, when enabled, will prevent the addition of a return type field if the annotation is 'None'. The implementation should isolate this conditional logic to only affect cases where autodoc_typehints is set to 'description', ensuring that the return type is omitted when appropriate.
feature1.entrypoint: File: sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py; Function: modify_field_list. Modify the function signature to include an additional parameter 'suppress_rtype' (defaulting to False) and adjust the block that adds the return type field so that it skips adding the field when suppress_rtype is True and the annotation is 'None'.

feature2.prompt: Using autodoc_typehints = "description" in Sphinx causes the autoclass directive to include a return type in the generated documentation, even though classes such as the Square class should not show any return type. The desired behavior is to have no return type displayed for class documentation, resulting in clearer and more accurate output. This feature is concerned with integrating the suppression mechanism into the overall process of merging type hints so that class objects are handled correctly.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature involves modifying the merge_typehints function so that it correctly leverages the new suppression capability. The implementation should detect when the object being processed is a class and then call modify_field_list with suppress_rtype set to True. The integration must ensure that the new parameter is passed along appropriately so that the resultant documentation omits the return type, aligning with the expected behavior.
feature2.entrypoint: File: sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py; Function: merge_typehints. Locate the section where modify_field_list is invoked and update it so that, for objects of type 'class', the function is called with suppress_rtype=True. This conditional adjustment is critical for ensuring that class-related documentation does not include an unwanted return type.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: The sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py file, including both the modify_field_list and merge_typehints functions, as well as the annotations data structure used for processing type hints.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 introduces the suppress_rtype parameter in the modify_field_list function, while Feature2 ensures that merge_typehints correctly passes suppress_rtype=True when handling class objects. Both parts must be merged and tested together to ensure that the return type suppression propagates properly through the documentation generation process.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers implementing each feature should coordinate on the naming and behavior of the suppress_rtype parameter, discuss the appropriate conditions under which the suppression logic should be activated, and review the integration points to ensure compatibility between the modifications in modify_field_list and merge_typehints.
